articleTitle: A Review of BMW iX3 Power Module - Part 1: Inner Configuration, Die Attachment, Busbar Connection and Encapsulation
abstract: The advancement of packaging of power modules is required to make improvements to electric vehicle drivetrains. This paper presents an independent review of the power module in a BMW iX3 inverter. The overall layout of the power module manufactured by Fuji Electric will be shown. Each half bridge uses two reverse conducting insulated gate bipolar transistors (RC-IGBTs) in parallel. The conventional wire bonding approach has been abandoned in favor of copper clip interconnections. The bonding mechanism of the bare dies, busbars and copper clips is also analyzed. The use of mold resin as encapsulation will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Over 25-GHz Bandwidth Testing Station Using a 0.3-mm-Pitch LGA Interface for a 50-Gbaud × 16-Channel CPO Transceiver
abstract: We report a design and characteristics of an electrical pluggable interface and a testing station for a 50- Gbaud x 16-channel CPO transceiver using a 0.3-mm-pitch LGA interface. This testing station has a 3-dB bandwidth of 27.1 GHz at the longest differential transmission line, which is sufficient for 50-Gbaud signal transmission. We also build an optical link employing a 53-Gbaud x 8-channel optical transceiver on the testing station to evaluate signal transmission characteristics. When operating the optical link by 53-Gbaud NRZ signals, a measured jitter margin at BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–12</sup>is as wide as 0.25 U.I. without any CDR and feed-forward equalizer.

articleTitle: Heat Assisted Magnetic Recording - Ultra-dense Laser and Plasmonic Component Integration to Increase Storage Density on Magnetic Media
abstract: In this paper we introduce Heat Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR), which is a radical method of increasing storage density on spinning magnetic media in hard disk drives. HAMR requires highly dense integration of a laser, optical waveguide and plasmonic resonator along with other photonic and magnetic components into an area no larger than 0.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> on a rapidly moving recording head. HAMR therefore embodies the most dense heterogenous photonic packaging subsystem ever developed.

articleTitle: Recent Progress and Task of GaN Materials and Devices for Power Applications
abstract: GaN is suitable for high-power electronic devices due to its high electron mobility and high breakdown voltage. In high-frequency devices, it is already being mass-produced for base stations and radars, and the development of materials and devices for future high-frequency devices is progressing. In power switching devices, low-power battery chargers have already been made smaller and more efficient, and vertical devices are being developed to achieve even higher power. In addition to device design and processes, the development of the material itself is necessary.

articleTitle: Five-sided Protection of the Chip with Bump Support Film Impact Resistance
abstract: A new BSF which can protect multi-sides (MP-BSF) is developed. By softening the hardness, the MP-BSF layer can embed the dicing kerf with no air bubbles. With MP-BSF, the chip can be protected from impact compared to the normal Si chip.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Self Assembly Using Copper Nano Film Formed by Blue Laser for Die-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding
abstract: In this study we investigated the structure of copper nano film on the glass chip as simulated wafer after blue laser irradiation in order to realize the hydrophilic copper pad for self assembly of die-to-wafer hybrid bonding.

articleTitle: High Reliability Solutions of EMI Shielding Technology for Advanced SiP Module
abstract: More and more wireless connectivity device market into Internet of Things (IoT) devices developing towards diversification. For connectivity functions including Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, 5G and wireless communication to support the requirement form consumer electronics, smart home, smart city, industrial and automotive applications. During wireless transmission from product to product by specific working frequency such as Wi-Fi with 2.4 to 5GHz. For new generation of Wi-Fi7 which are utilizing additional 6 GHz (5.925 to 7.125 GHz) frequency bands to support a transmission rate up to 9.6 to 46 Gbps. By using higher frequency to get better data rate communication between device to user, so the EMI (Electromagnetic Interference) noise is key challenge which will cause an electrical phenomenon when electromagnetic waves interfere to another device and cause the signal degradation, signal data failure. To meet the EMI shielding protection requirement, the SiP module could integrate mulit-IC/package, multi-passive components, and antenna design with molding then apply EMI shielding solutions to get small form factor and reduce signal noise for connectivity product. In this paper, we select different EMI shielding material to compare each frequency band status and use simulation tool to create model to evaluate the shielding Effectiveness (SE) performance comparison. To design a EMI shielding test vehicle (TV) which include a micro-strip line antenna to collect SE performance and proceed assembly molding and sputter coating process, then mount the shielding TV on PCB board to do signal measurement by near field scanner during the shielding room. We compare the result between with and without sputter coating sample to calculate the SE performance and check with simulation correction data. Based on difference sputter coating material (such as Stainless steel=SUS and Titanium=Ti). Ti material is good adhesion material compare with SUS to enhance the peeling test result during SiP module reliability collection. Finally, this paper will demonstrate advanced SiP module with high reliability EMI shielding solutions for future connectivity devices application.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Analysis of Polarization Dependent Polymer Optical Waveguide Characteristics
abstract: We design a measurement system to evaluate polarization dependent characteristics of polymer optical waveguides fabricated by the Mosquito method to be applied to a coupler between a single-mode fiber and silicon photonics chip. We observe the dependence of birefringence in single-mode polymer waveguides on their numerical aperture.

articleTitle: Design of Compact ECU with Two-Layer Daughter Board Structure for Automotive High-Performance Computing
abstract: We proposed a new two-layer daughter board structure to balance both high performance and compact size in electrical control unit (ECU). The structure separates interface board and processor board for high-density implementation. We concluded the structure can realize cooling capacity of over 300 W, signal integrity of 6 Gbps, and the chassis size reduction of more than 20 %.

articleTitle: In-Line SEM Evaluation Technique for Cu Pad Nanotopography for Hybrid Bonding Applications
abstract: Wafer hybrid bonding is an essential technology for 3D integration of semiconductors. This technology involves directly bonding Cu pads formed on wafers. Considering the bulging out of Cu during annealing, the height of the Cu pad is controlled to be recessed by a few nanometers from the SiCN dielectric layer using Chemical Mechanical Processing (CMP) process. In wafer bonding, significant recess amounts due to Cu galvanic corrosion and recess amount variations of Cu pads affect the bonding quality. Therefore, we have developed a Cu pad evaluation technique, specifically focusing on rapid inspection of corrosions and measurement of recess amount using in-line scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with four backscattered electron (BSE) detectors arranged in different orientations. Verification with 350 nm-sized pads confirmed the inspection of galvanic corrosion and the ability to measure height with a precision of 0.47 nm in root mean square errors. This SEM-based Cu pad inspection and measurement technique using four BSE detectors can be utilized for controlling Cu height in wafer bonding through CMP.

articleTitle: High-Bandwidth Optical Transmission with Single External Laser Source (ELS) and Polymer Splitters for Co-packaged Optics
abstract: We demonstrated high-bandwidth optical transmission using a polymer-based 1×4 splitter and a single external laser source (ELS) with an extremely high power of +20 dBm per channel, potentially achieving a bandwidth of 4.0 Tbps.

articleTitle: Ultra High Optical Output Power 8-Channel ELS Module Employing a Blind Mate Optical Connector for Co-Packaged Optics
abstract: We design an ultra-high-power class (i.e., +23 ± 1.5 dBm/channel) uncooled ELS module employing a blind mate optical connector. Then, we report characteristics of the + 23-dBm x 8-channel ELS module in a practical air-cooling condition.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of Factor Effect on Transient Thermal Test Performance for Electronic Power Devices
abstract: This research uses Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to study the impact of different factors on Thermal Performance of Electronic Power Devices during Transient Thermal Test (TTT), including top metal thickness, bond wire diameter, and bond ball shape. The FEA results are also compared with experiment results.

articleTitle: Fabrication of a Glass Sub-Mount with High Heat Dissipation
abstract: We developed a glass sub-mount with thermal vias for EMLs, achieving comparable thermal performance to AlN and high-frequency capability, demonstrated by 53.2 GHz bandwidth and successful PAM4 signal transmission.

articleTitle: Evaluation of MPI Suppression by Bending a Short PMF Cable Attached to an ELS Module
abstract: We investigate the generation of MPI and its suppression by bending a pigtail fiber cable attached to an ELS module. Experiments are implemented for 1.0-m and 0.3-m PMFs considered to a length range in an actual usage. MPI is strongly generated when the PMF is straightened. When applying bending conditions in an actual usage, an MPI value is reduced as low as <-40 dB. As a result, it is concluded that MPI can be sufficiently suppressed for pigtailed-ELS modules.

articleTitle: Effect of Microstructure on the Electromigration Performance of 2- μm-Cu Redistribution Line under In-situ SEM Observation
abstract: A specialized experiment method for in-situ video investigation of the electromigration behavior in fine line Cu RDL has been established in this study. A Kelvin structure design features electroplated Cu RDL straight-line structure, with polyimide passivation removed via a plasma-decap process and surfaces polished using a FIB. The experiments were conducted at a high current density of 2 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a temperature of 77°C to accelerate the electro migration process. During the investigation, voids were observed to form and grow on the cathode side at the triple joint of the grain boundary, while hillocks accumulated on the anode side. Two types of Cu RDLs were electroplated using different electroplating solutions, and their microstructures were analyzed using EBSD, while mechanical properties were assessed with a pico-indenter system. The lifetime of Cu RDLs with smaller copper grains was found to be approximately seven times longer than that of those with larger grains. The superior lifetime could be attributed to improved mechanical properties and a greater number of grain boundaries, which serve to impede the movement of voids (or atoms). These findings suggest that reducing grain size is an effective strategy for enhancing the electromigration performance of fine line RDLs in high current density environments.

articleTitle: Development of Through Semiconductor via Manufacturing Process for Heterogeneous Integration of GaN Power Device on Si-LSI
abstract: The sample was prepared by bonding the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>surfaces of a GaN device and a Si device. The bonding sample was etched from the (111)Si side, which is the supporting substrate of the GaN device, to create a TSV (Through Semiconductor Via). By optimizing each process, it was achieved a TSV with a smooth bottom surface at the bonding sample.

articleTitle: 3D Polymer Optical Waveguide-based Fan-in/out Device for Silicon Photonics Chips
abstract: To realize a subminiature low-loss adiabatic coupler to silicon photonics chips, we design a PMT connector- integrated polymer waveguide device with circular single- mode cores to fabricate it using the Mosquito method.

articleTitle: Fixed Connection of Single-Mode Polymer Optical Waveguide with Single-Mode Optical Fiber
abstract: We demonstrate forming a waveguide module by adhering a core in a polymer waveguide and a single-mode fiber (SMF) to stabilize the connection at high temperature. We confirm that the connections are stably maintained at 86°C.

articleTitle: EMC Overview, Causes and Physics
abstract: An overview of EMC (Electro-Magnetic-Compatibility), emission tests are given. Direct causes and physics of conducted and radiated noise tests are discussed. Root causes and physics are discussed, for wires, micro-strip-lines, slots in ground-plane..

articleTitle: Direct Connection of Multimode Polymer Waveguide and Multimode Fibers Using the Mosquito Method
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the monomer dispensing conditions for the Mosquito method to accurately arrange the cores on the desired positions. Then, direct connection of waveguide core and multimode fiber is realized with the Mosquito method.

articleTitle: Diagnosing PCB(A) Deficiencies in Medical Instruments During Reprocessing and Sterilization Cycles
abstract: Medical devices and instruments used in surgical procedures require sterilization and cleaning to allow their use in multiple surgeries. Any device or instrument that comes in contact with the patient, or has exposure to biological materials, requires cleaning and sterilization as a standard protocol before they can be used again. Removal of all biological materials, pathogens, debris, and contaminants from the medical device is an absolute requirement. The sterilization procedures may involve the use of harsh chemicals, high temperatures and moisture, high pressure environments, as well as vibrational frequencies, not necessarily all together. These methods have a detrimental effect on the life of the electronics included in the medical devices. These requirements are unlike anything that product life testing of electronics in the consumer and industrial fields will encounter. As such, most electronics used in medical devices face conditions which they were never explicitly designed for. Traditionally, most medical instruments that faced such reprocessing, either had very limited electronics, or had limited usage of high-density PCB (Printed Circuit Board) technologies which would be subjected to multiple such reprocessing cycles. Surgical endoscopes used in Robotic Surgeries are the exception, as they require high density, high complexity electronics packaged tightly within very small spaces (5mm-8mm diameter tubes) and are required to survive and function after undergoing multiple rounds of reprocessing and sterilization. Such an application exposes deficiencies and limitations of PCB technologies in a manner not seen in typical consumer or industrial applications. This paper seeks to highlight the unique challenges faced by PCB's and electronic components under such sterilization regimes. It also seeks to identify best design practices and technologies in PCB manufacturing for such applications, and identify what should be avoided.

articleTitle: A Review of BMW iX3 Power Module - Part 2: Stacked-Plate Fin Heatsink Structure
abstract: This paper introduces a heatsink structure employed in the power module of the BMW iX3 traction inverter. The heatsink features a stacked-plate configuration with single-sided cooling. Two distinct patterns of perforated plates are stacked alternately to direct coolant flow and enhance heat exchange performance. Geometric specifications are analyzed in detail and several related patents are reviewed to investigate heat exchange performance in a relation to various heatsink design parameters. Pressure loss is examined using Ansys Fluent simulation.

articleTitle: High-Performance Flip-Chip BGA Packages Reliability Prediction in Automotive Applications
abstract: Recently, the demand of IC Packages has grown rapidly in automotive applications. Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) require more powerful and more chips to enable Level 2 and higher systems. However, automotive package operates in severer environment than consumer package, so it requires higher reliability whether in package-level or board-level reliability tests. To ensure packages reliability, a more comprehensive approach needs to be implemented. In this study, our aim is to predict high-performance flip-chip BGA (HFCBGA) substrate copper trace fatigue life in temperature cyclic test (TCT). HFCBGA is the composite package of FCBGA with heat spreader that is used to extend the heat conduction area and enhance package warpage control because of its high power and high speed demand. We used advanced Metrology Analyzer (aMA) to measure package warpage especially from TCT condition - 55°C to 125°C and then used finite element method (FEM) to establish 3-D numerical model for validation. Afterwards, we built up a detailed sub-model to simulate substrate copper trace plastic work density (PWD) considering Anand's model under thermal cycling, and brought the PWD increment into Coffin-Manson Model to predict substrate copper trace fatigue life. From the simulation results, we can get the key factors affecting substrate copper trace fatigue life. Through different structure designs and BOM selection such as heat spreader designs, adhesive types, soldermask types, trace layout, etc., substrate copper trace broken risk can be lowest to meet automotive specification of AEC - Q100.

articleTitle: Development of Optical Microneedle Lens Array to Deliver Light Efficiently for Photodynamic Therapy to Treat Basal Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Here, optical microneedle-lens-array for the photodynamic therapy of skin cancer were developed. Computer simulations have demonstrated improved light transmission in the skin. Finally, the microneedles were successfully coated with a specific quantity of the photosensitizer.

articleTitle: Fluxless Low-Temperature Flip Chip Solder Interconnect for Cost Reduction
abstract: This paper studies low temperature Sn- Bi solder as interconnect material for flip chip bonding on Trace-in-bump (TIB). The results demonstrated that the flip chip to TIB bonding using Sn- Bi solder is feasible. The micro-analysis showed that intermetallic compound (IMC) layer formation consisted of Sn, Au, and Ni with good electrical connection. The interconnect system survived the reliability test conditions for application with no crack or delamination was observed. This indicated the low temperature Sn- Bi solder in the TIB interconnect structure with the underfill material was able to overcome the brittleness and demonstrated the ability to survive the package integrity test. This provides opportunities in reduction of packaging cost through material cost, carbon footprint and package thermal stresses due to lower temperature soldering process.

articleTitle: Post-Fab Laser Trimming: Increasing Yield and Lowering Power Consumption of PICs
abstract: In recent years photonics has received a lot of attention as a way to extend the growth of semiconductor devices beyond the boundaries of the Moore's Law. PICs (Photonics Integrated Chips) are now being used in interconnects to enable high-speed data transfer between components, reducing latency and energy consumption particularly in datacenters and telecommunications systems. While wafer yields of mature semiconductor technologies have reached figures higher than 98%, yields in photonics are much lower. The paper presents a laser-based post fabrication method for recovering imperfect PICs, as well as the basic concepts for the automation that is necessary for an economically viable process.

articleTitle: Thermally Stable Solder Resist for High Temperature Applications
abstract: This paper introduces a new dry film type solder resist (DFSR) material designed for automotive package applications. This material achieves high reliability by mitigating the stress caused by temperature changes suppressing the occurrence of cracks.

articleTitle: Development of Re-assemblable Multifiber Connector for Co-Packaged Optics
abstract: A molded product multifiber connector is developed. The connector can be reassembled before and after the reflow process. Evaluation results show that the connector can provide similar performance as a standard MPO connector with a smaller footprint.

articleTitle: Sequential Surface Treatment Process with VUV light and Ar Plasma for Room Temperature Au-Au Bonding
abstract: We have demonstrated room-temperature pressureless bonding of wafers with smooth Au thin films in air using a sequential surface treatment process with VUV light followed by Ar plasma.

articleTitle: Study on the Novel Fabrication Procedure of Polyimide Multilayer Circuits for a Space Transformer of DRAM Probe Card using Parallel Build-up Process
abstract: The space transformer plays a critical role in DRAM probe cards for on-wafer testing of semiconductor chips. Typically, it comprises a multilayer ceramic (MLC) substrate and a multilayer thin film (MTF) circuit based on polyimide. The conventional method of MTF fabrication involves a sequential thin-film build-up process. While this technique can achieve fine conductor lines and small via-holes, it is associated with prolonged delivery times and increased costs due to low yields from circuit defects and layer deformations. In this research, we investigated an innovative parallel build-up process that employs TPI (thermoplastic polyimide)-coated polyimide (PI) films and a Cu-based low-temperature sinterable paste. Via-holes and trenched circuit patterns were generated using laser drilling and scribing methods, followed by filling with a sinterable paste and laminating at temperatures over 270°C in a vacuum press. This approach successfully fabricated MTF composed of a polyimide multilayer circuit board (PI-MCB) with more than 10 dielectric layers, which was integrated onto a 5mm-thick alumina substrate with a spin-coated adhesive layer on its surface by a vacuum press. The results suggest that this novel fabrication procedure is applicable to enhance the MTF manufacturing method of space transformers for DRAM probe cards, offering increased efficiency and cost savings compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Structural Investigation of Microchannel and Optical Waveguide Co-integrated Sensor Devices
abstract: In this paper, we design a device that integrates a microchannel and optical waveguide core, and fabricate it using the Mosquito method. Then, the light output is detected from the core after transmitting through the microchannel.

articleTitle: Towards Scalable Aligned Two-Photon Lithography for Photonic Integration
abstract: This paper presents advancements in aligned two-photon lithography (A2PL), where high resolution laser-based 3D fabrication technology is combined with high precision alignment routines. We demonstrate both camera- and confocal-based 3D detection algorithms for high-precision alignment, achieving accuracies below 100 nm. Two-photon lithography is utilized to fabricate photonic components such as micro-lenses for fiber-to-chip coupling, with losses as low as 1.7 dB and out-of-plane coupling structures. The workflow is readily adapted to other applications and material platforms, enabling scalable additive and multi-material fabrication.

articleTitle: Loss Reduction of Single-mode Y-branched Polymer Optical Waveguide for MUX/DEMUX Devices in Mode Division Multiplexing Links
abstract: Using the Mosquito method, we fabricate asymmetric single-mode Y-branched waveguides applicable to MUX/DEMUX devices for MDM technology. In order to reduce the insertion loss of Y-branched waveguides, we reexamine the fabrication conditions of symmetric single-mode Y-branched waveguides.

articleTitle: Socket Design for 1x4 mmWave Antenna in Package with Beamforming Testing
abstract: In this study, we present a 1x4 broadband dual-polarized antenna array built on a 10 (4+2+4) multilayer organic substrate and assessed with a test socket. The design comprises stacked patch antennas featuring parasitic elements to improve operating bandwidth, and the optimal substrate configuration was selected to ensure cost-effectiveness. Through the implementation of an effective grounding strategy for the parasitic elements, a short-circuit mirror-image current effect is achieved, which in turn results in a notable reduction in component area. Following optimization, the dimensions were reduced from 6.5 x 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>to 4.5 x 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, representing a 31% decrease. The test socket, comprising a load board and socket for the assessment of the antenna array's characteristics, enables the measurement of the antenna array's realised gain in both vertical and horizontal polarisation within the 26.5 to 29.5 GHz range, with values ranging from 7 to 9 dBi.

articleTitle: Novel Additive Manufacturing Platform for Freeform 3D Microelectronics and Packaging
abstract: Additive manufacturing of electronics offers new possibilities and functionalities for structural electronics and chip package design. Here we present our novel 3D microelectronics printing platform and a test setup to characterise printed electrical circuitry.

articleTitle: Enhancing Adhesion and Peel Strength for Fine Line Design on FCCSP Package
abstract: This study investigates the critical factors influencing the adhesion performance of FCCSP substrates, focusing on enhancing fine-line designs. By systematically examining the effects of filler content in Bismaleimide-Triazine (BT) resin, copper foil surface roughness, and baking conditions, we identified key parameters that significantly improve the peel strength between the prepreg (PP) layer and the electroless copper layer. The results indicate that reducing filler content, optimizing surface roughness, and implementing specific baking processes enhance mechanical adhesion and substrate reliability, thereby supporting fine-line pitch down to 22 μm while maintaining high peel strength. The findings demonstrate the potential of the FCCSP process, independent of the Electroless Semi-Additive Process (eSAP), to meet stringent industry requirements for high-density electronic packaging. This study provides a cost-effective and reliable pathway for advancing FCCSP technology, meeting the growing demands for miniaturization and multifunctionality in modern electronic devices.

articleTitle: Quantum Co-packaged Optical Assembly
abstract: Packaging of QPICs requires low-loss coupling between fiber arrays and PICs. As QPICs typically operate on entangled or single photons, coupling is more critical than for conventional PICs, in which thousands of photons are manipulated at a time. In this paper we will report on the results from the UK government funded projects, in which a novel metallic aspherical micro-mirror array unit was coupled for the first time to a QPIC. The micro-mirror array is formed in a stamping process allowing it to be produced in high-volume and it can be deployed in diverse environments including high temperature or cryogenic environments.

articleTitle: Adhesion Between Si Substrates in Liquid Water Using Inorganic Polymer
abstract: In this study, Si/Si pairs were bonded underwater using perhydropolysilazane(PHPS), and the bonding strengths were measured and peeled surfaces were analyzed. As a result, high-strength bonding was obtained while promoting silica conversion of PHPS.

articleTitle: Heat Dissipation Study of Sub-THz Band AiP Module
abstract: To address the increased heat density from high-density implementation for the 6G era, we examined the structure of sub-THz band AiP modules. We found that incorporating heat dissipation structures such as thermal vias and bumps into the AiP modules reduces their thermal resistance by about 20 K/W. Furthermore, we verified the heat dissipation in use cases such as mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Oxide Microtubes Fabrication with 10μm to 5μm Pitches and Assembly Characterization
abstract: This paper presents design and fabrication process of metallized oxide microtubes at 10μm, 7.5μm and 5μm pitches and assembly at room temperature of the pitch ones. Morphological and electrical characterization have been investigated.

articleTitle: Implementation of Curved CMOS Image Sensors by Transferring Silicon-On-Insulator Layers
abstract: We present curved complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor image sensors using silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technologies. A 11-µm-thick SOI layer was curved into a cylindrical concave shape. The sensor successfully captured video images while effectively correcting lens aberrations.

Author Keywords: curved complementary metal-oxide- semiconductor image sensor

articleTitle: Multi-channel Integration of Polymer Spot Size Expander on Silicon Photonics Chip
abstract: Multi-channel integration of miniaturized polymer spot size expanders fabricated using UV-curable resin on a “silicon base plate” is newly proposed. The feasibility of the proposed structure was studied theoretically and was shown by primary experiment.

articleTitle: High Density, High Bandwidth Copper Interconnects to Support High Density IC Packaging
abstract: As package interconnect bandwidth and density increase, so do the signal integrity challenges to transmit the signals through the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) with sufficient performance to allow for the use of low latency forward error correction (FEC). While this can be done by increasing electrical power or by using high-cost low-loss PCB materials, a favorable alternative is to use of copper cables to transmit the signal directly from chip to chip, chip to backplane, or chip to front panel. These low-loss copper cables take the signal off the PCB, allowing data to be transmitted over longer distances while using less drive power than if it were to be carried over PCB traces.

articleTitle: 3.2T Co-Package Optics (CPO) Module Based on 200G/ch Silicon-Organic-Hybrid (SOH) Mach-Zehnder Modulator (MZM)
abstract: In this work, we will show experimental data of high-speed MZM PIC in module level at 100G/ch and simulated data of SOH-MZM at 200G/ch to prove this SOH-PIC technology is capable for 200G/ch CPO application.

articleTitle: A Study on Reducing Crosstalk by Efficiently Placing Guard Vias
abstract: Press-fit connector is mounted on the Through Hole (TH)s, which cause large crosstalk. Guard vias are required to reduce crosstalk. Our purpose is to clarify the effective placement of guard vias and THs. It was shown that crosstalk can be reduced 35.7 dB by placing the guard via on the central axis of the Victim and shifting the Victim by approximately 4/5 times the distance between the signal THs.

articleTitle: Bend-Optimized Optical Fiber with Low Multipath Interference in the O-Band
abstract: This paper summarizes the design of a new fiber optimized for co-packaged optics and presents data on developmental prototypes that demonstrates their suitability for use in short-length optical interconnects operating at 1310 nm. Guidelines are provided for establishing a minimum bend radius for cable routing which prevents both the optical loss and the probability of a fiber break from exceeding predetermined limits.

articleTitle: Sintered Ag & Cu Based Die Attach for Power Package and Power Module Application
abstract: Sintered bonding technology will be required to achieve higher thermal conductivity and higher joint reliability for power package and power module application. Several characteristic sintered materials have been confirmed for joint reliability.

articleTitle: German License Plate Recognition System Using the YoloV8 Model and EasyOCR
abstract: License Plate Recognition (LPR) is a highly valuable technology for the modern road-infrastructure, which can accommodate wide-range features. This paper focuses on developing a German License Plate Recognition (LPR) using the technology of the YOLOv8 model and EasyOCR recognition technology. The Python programming language and OpenCV image-processing library are used to develop this system whereas the EasyOCR library is used as an OCR for recognizing characters. The proposed system developed to detect different license plates for a video input and at the same time recognizes both characters and numbers combination for these detected plates. This hybrid mechanism improves performance and accuracy of the detection process by the combination of simultaneous detection and recognition of each license plate for each frame. The over 4000 images of vehicles and German license plates are used as a dataset of this research. By using the YOLOv8 model and EasyOCR recognition model, a license plate detection rate of 95% and a recognition rate of 94% have been achieved on the test results. These results indicate the success of the proposed detection and recognition process on the German Car license Plate.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Analysis and Design for HBM3 on Silicon-Based 2.5D Packaging
abstract: In this paper, a method is proposed to fast evaluate die to die channel design in 2.5D silicon-based packages to reduce the layout cycle time. To verify that the design obtained through this method can meet the high-speed requirements of High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Gen3 at data rates of 6.4 Gbps and 7.2 Gbps, interconnect models are extracted using a 3D simulation tool, and time-domain analysis is conducted to confirm the eye diagram performance. This ensures an efficient design process, resulting in designs that can support the signal demands of HBM Gen3.

articleTitle: Application of EMC Simulation Including Semiconductor for Short-term Development
abstract: Automotive EMC environment has become complex recently. This paper proposes EMC simulation model structure, consisting of test setup, ECU, and semiconductor. Applying the proposed model structure i s practical to satisfy with requirements and short-term development.

articleTitle: Al Wiring and Cu Wiring Connection by Newly Established AL Ribbon Stack Bonding Technology for Power Package and Module
abstract: For low RDS (drain-source on-resistance) required for future automotive devices, a newly Al ribbon stacked technology was established in which Al ribbon is placed on top of Al pad and connected Al or Cu wire.

articleTitle: Wearable Electronic Packaging Technology for VR and Biomedical Applications
abstract: We have been researching wearable devices and their packaging technologies for VR and medical devices. Specifically, for VR, we have developed wearable devices that integrate motors and sensors into clothing to be used alongside VR visuals. On the other hand, we have developed technologies to integrate and make wearable devices for electrocardiograms, electromyograms, and even ultrasound probes into clothing. In this invited lecture, we will introduce these recent studies.

articleTitle: Formation of Au Hollow Micro-Bump Arrays for Low Temperature Au-Au Bonding
abstract: Au hollow micro-bump arrays that plastically deform and facilitate low temperature Au-Au bonding were developed. The bump arrays were fabricated by Au film transfer method based on template stripping and surface activated bonding.

articleTitle: A Novel of Ultra Thinner Thermoelectric Device for Wireless Sensor Application
abstract: A flexible thermoelectric generator (FT-TEG) was fabricated by original ink formulation and screen- printing method. Thermoelectric (TE) element size was optimized based on heat flux calculations, and a wireless sensor application with the FT-TEG was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Simulation and Fabrication of Highly Bendable Advanced 3D Corrugated Interconnects Using Flexible FOWLP
abstract: This paper focuses on the simulation and fabrication of advanced 3D corrugated wires used for an integrated wearable device platform called in-mold flexible hybrid electronics (iFHE) fabricated in die-first FOWLP processing using PDMS as a substrate. Conventional 3D corrugated wires follow the rule of going straight ahead on the XY plane with a vertical wavy shape of serpentine or trapezoid on the flexible substrate. To enhance the bendability of the conventional 3D corrugated wires, the advanced 3D wires combine horizontal meander shapes used in traditional 2D wires with the vertical corrugated shape used in the conventional 3D wires. This paper verifies the effectiveness of the advanced 3D corrugated structure from simulation aspects and demonstrates the fabrication of the advanced 3D corrugated wires.

articleTitle: Verification of Dicing Method for Silicon Photonic Wafers
abstract: We prepared SiPh chips diced by two different dicing methods and tried optical connection of each chip to FAs (Fiber Array). We evaluated the end-face conditions and optical characteristics of these chips.

articleTitle: Comparative Studies on the Reliability and Intermetallic Integrity of Novel Au-Coated Ag Versus Cu and Au Bonding Wires
abstract: The reliability of Au-coated Ag (ACA) wire is investigated and compared with Au and Cu wires. Interfacial analyses revealed that the IMC of the bonded ACA wire is as robust as that of Au and Cu wires and passed the standard reliability tests for automotive.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Transmission Line Properties on Si-CMOS Chip by Probe Backside Reflection Method in Millimeter-Wave Frequencies
abstract: In this study, we demonstrate the evaluation of effective dielectric constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\text{eff}})$</tex> and quality factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{Q})$</tex> of transmission lines (TLs) on a Si-CMOS chip using the probe backside reflection (PBR) method in the frequency range up to 220 GHz. The both properties are known to be influenced by distribution of dummy metals around a TL as well as dimensions of a TL. The PBR method is expected to reduce occupied chip area compares to the conventional thru-reflect-line (TRL) method, because the PBR method requires only one co-planar waveguide (CPW) for the evaluation. Three types of the TLs with different cross-sectional structures were designed, and those <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\text{eff}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{Q}$</tex> were evaluated by the PBR method. These results were qualitatively corresponded to the simulation results. Relationship between measurement accuracy and occupied chip area was compared to the conventional TRL method. The PBR method has a possibility to reduce occupied chip area for evaluation of the TL properties.

articleTitle: New PFAS-Free Optical Adhesive with High Heat Resistance and Low Refractive Index
abstract: The study presents a new, PFAS(per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances)-free optical adhesive for data center optical connections. Its low refractive index, high transmittance, and high heat resistance make it effective at reducing optical transmission loss and environmental impact.

articleTitle: Multichip-to-Wafer Mini-LED Bonding Technology for Photobiomodulation Sheet Devices Using Flexible FOWLP
abstract: This paper focuses on flexible hybrid electronics (FHE) fabrication with small dies embedded in a hydrogel flexible substrate based on a redistribution layer (RDL)-first fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP) methodology for low-power light therapy called photobiomodulation (PBM). The near-infrared (NIR) mini-LEDs integrated with the hydrogel substrate irradiate tissues with NIR light, promoting chemical reactions within cells and producing analgesic, anti-inflammatory., and tissue regeneration effects. The focus of this study is to lower the bonding temperature and improve the bonding yield of the NIR mini-LEDs in the chip-to-wafer bonding process. Cu/Sn microbumps and a unique ACF (anisotropic conductive film) were employed to enhance the low-temperature repetitive bondabilities.

articleTitle: Co-Design of Photonic IC, Electronic IC, and Interposer for 1.6 Tbps O/E Converter in Active Optical Package
abstract: We have developed a design methodology for a compact and high-speed optical/electrical converter for active optical package through co-design of a photonic integrated circuit and electronic integrated circuits, assembled with an organic redistribution layer interposer.

articleTitle: Polymer Optical Waveguide for Silicon Photonics
abstract: In this paper, we report on the features of optical waveguide components using our materials for single-mode polymer optical waveguides intended for applications in CPO (Co-Packaged optics) and other fields. We also highlight the advantages of fluoropolymer materials and discuss the required characteristics for optical communication components.

articleTitle: Impact of Laser Welding on Assembly of Printed Circuit Boards in Medical Devices
abstract: Reusable medical devices play a crucial role in healthcare, but their reliability hinges on robust assembly processes. Their failure during usage can be catastrophic. These devices face aggressive sterilization procedures, exposure to harsh chemicals, and extreme temperature fluctuations. Assembling printed circuit boards (PCBs) into mechanical subsystems introduces subtle failure mechanisms that often elude traditional manufacturing quality control processes. Unfortunately, these latent defects become more pronounced during device usage or storage, exacerbated by thermal variations, vibrations, and mechanical shocks. The need to seal, hermetically or otherwise, for medical devices stems from their use in repeated surgeries. Biohazard safety requires that the medical instruments are capable of being functionally connected to the surgical system to perform its primary purpose, while at the same time remain internally isolated from the environment that they are operating in. This becomes particularly relevant due to the need for sterilization and cleaning procedures to allow their use in multiple surgeries. When an electronic assembly in a medical device like an edge card or connector, which is needed to be available and accessible outside the sealed region to contact the rest of the surgical system, it faces the issue of defining and controlling an ‘exposed’ area which contains the edge card fingers', while isolating the rest of the electronics in a hermetic or sealed zone. The interface region for such a transition is often sealed with a combination of soldering, epoxy sealing and welding. When applying welding as a sealing approach in combination with the other approaches, the relative movements, and expansions of the dissimilar materials lead to unexpected failure modes and effects. This paper aims to address the challenges associated with laser welding during PCB assembly in medical devices. We investigate process variations in laser welding and discuss how these factors exacerbate underlying defects. By analyzing failure modes and conducting thorough failure analysis, we provide insights into mitigating these vulnerabilities. The findings are particularly relevant for industries where the robustness of printed circuit assemblies (PCAs) directly influences device performance and patient safety.

articleTitle: Field-Size Converter for Edge Coupling of Multimode LD to Thin Film Waveguide
abstract: An inverse-taper comb structure is proposed and designed to couple a visible multimode LD to a 150-nm-thick Si-N waveguide. The efficiencies of field size conversion were predicted to be higher than -0.02 dB for red, green, and blue LDs.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Compact 106-Gb/s PAM4 × 8-Channel Linear-Drive VCSEL-Based Transceiver for Co-Packaged Optics
abstract: We report a design and optical link characteristics of an ultra-compact 106-Gb/s PAM4 × 8-channel linear-drive VCSEL-based transceiver for Co-Packaged Optics. This optical transceiver employs the record narrowest 0.3-mm-pitch LGA for the electrical interface. To expand the bandwidth, we use a core-less building-up multi-layer organic substrate to avoid impedance mismatch of the vias in the core layer. A 3-dB bandwidth of the differential lines is as wide as >53 GHz based on an electromagnetic simulation. When operating the optical transceiver with a bit stream of 106-Gb/s PAM4 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>-1 PRBSQ in a loopback optical link without any CDR functionalities, BER measures less than the KP4-FEC threshold for both serial and 8-channel operations.

articleTitle: Design of Thin-film Narrowband Retroreflector for Oblique Incidence of Diverging Wave
abstract: Focusing cavity-resonator-integrated guided- mode resonance filters for oblique incidence were designed to serve as external cavity mirrors integrated. Distributions of coupling coefficients were discussed for high retroreflectance. Retroreflectances higher than 60% were predicted by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Effect of Sb Dopant in Growth of r-GeO2 Thin Films
abstract: Sb doped rutile-GeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>thin films were grown on rutile- Ti02 substrates varying the growth temperatures. The sample grown under 700°C shows FWHM of XRC as 694 arcsec.

articleTitle: 13th IEEE CPMT Symposium Japan (ICSJ2024) Committee Members
Message from the General Chair
abstract: On behalf of the ICSJ2024 organizing committee, I would like to express our sincere appreciation to all the participants for their dedicated contributions to the conference. We are very pleased to welcome all of you, and also very proud to be able to host the 13th conference at Ritsumeikan University Suzaku Campus, in Kyoto. “IEEE CPMT Symposium Japan (ICSJ)” is one of the most widely recognized international conferences sponsored by the IEEE Electronics Packaging Society (EPS) and has been held annually in Kyoto in November. The conference was inaugurated in 1992 as “The VLSI Packaging Workshop in Japan (VPWJ)” to provide a platform for you to communicate and interact with global leaders in packaging technology. Later in 2010, the conference was renamed to “ICSJ”, and this year marks the 13th. ICSJ conference event, and 22nd conference since establishing VPWJ.
